newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA REFINANCING LOANS 11.3 PCT DOWN IN FEB.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA REFINANCING LOANS 11.3 PCT DOWN IN FEB.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) refinancing loans fell by 11.3 percent in February, with auctioned loans plunging to 563.4 billion lei from January's 1.4 trillion after tightened monetary policy, BNR data showed.

The average total daily refinancing was 6.2 trillion lei in February, when Lombard loans rose to 166.6 billion lei from 717 million in January as the money market faced chronical leu shortages following cuts in the BNR's one-week funds.

Over the past month the BNR has soaked liquidity from the market in a bid to combat rising inflation. Its moves triggered upswings in refinancing rates followed by a surge in commercial banks' deposit rates.

The BNR's auctioned credit rate soared to an all-time high of 426.5 percent last week from about 81 percent in early February, while the Lombard rate, which was allowed to float in line with the one-week rate, jumped to 682.4 percent from 90 percent a month ago.
Banks deposit rates climbed to an annual 150 percent for one-month deposits from about 40 percent in the New Year.
Year-on-year inflation quickened to 76.3 percent in January from 56.9 percent in December and is seen climbing in the next few months, led by fuel, power and food price rises.

Structural refinancing facilities, for which the BNR charges a discount rate of 50 percent, remained almost unchanged at 2.6 trillion lei, while soft loans for farmers fell by 6.2 percent to 962 billion in February.

The credits granted to debtors in litigation, respectively to troubled banks Dacia Felix SA and Renasterea Creditului Romanesc Credit Bank SA, froze at 1.87 trillion lei. The BNR does not charge interest on those loans.
Both banks, which revealed big debts and huge losses, await court rulings on their fate -- reorganisation or liquidation.
